To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the solar neutrino oscillation parameters are consistent with a neutrino mass hierarchy m_1 \lesssim m_2 \lesssim \sqrt{m_1^2 + m_3^2} with m_3 \sim \sqrt{\Delta m_{\rm atm}^2} \sim 0.05$ eV and that the atmospheric neutrino oscillation data are consistent with an inverted neutrino mass hierarchy with m_1 \sim m_2 \
the solar and atmospheric neutrinos can be explained simultaneously by the same set of neutrino oscillation parameters, and that there is a strong correlation among the parameters.

(a) The solar neutrino problem and the atmospheric neutrino problem can be solved in the same scenario by a single set of oscillation parameters, and that (b) the hierarchy of leptonic masses and the approximate decoup- ling of solar and atmospheric oscillations can be naturally reflected in the flavor mixing matrix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a phenomenological interpretation and a model-independent parametrization of atmospheric and solar oscillations.
the question of whether there exists a simple and natural interpretation of the observed atmospheric and solar neutrinos in terms of a unified model.
a phenomenological understanding of neutrino mixing parameters and a possible origin of the observed neutrino oscillations within the standard model of electroweak interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present neutrino oscillation data are consistent with both scenarios (a) and (b) and that a more precise and detailed understanding of the lepton mass spectrum and mixing matrix requires further experimental and phenomenological efforts.
the current neutrino oscillation data are not inconsistent with a flavor democracy ansatz for charged leptons, and with mass degeneracy ansatz for neutrinos.
, in the light of the current data, the neutrino mass spectra of both types (a) and (b) are allowed, but the former is more favored.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a new paradigm for neutrino physics, based on the concept of approximate flavor democracy, has been established.
the present neutrino oscillation data can be naturally explained by the lepton flavor mixing matrix which is a product of two rotation matrices, one for solar and the other for atmospheric neutrinos.
the neutrino mass matrix, in contrast to the charged lepton mass matrix, should be hierarchical, and the flavor mixing matrix should be hierarchical as well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a phenomenological interpretation can provide a useful guideline to the theoretical understanding of the neutrino sector.
the hierarchy of leptoquark masses is a key to the interpretation of neutrino oscillation experiments.
, if the neutrino mass hierarchy is normal, the solar and atmospheric neutrinos are not independent oscillators.
